page: Microsoft Azure D8pds_v5 is an ARM64-based virtual machine belonging to the DPDSv5 server family. It is powered by an Ampere Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 3.0 GHz, featuring 8 dedicated physical cores with 1 thread per core. The hardware configuration includes 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Additionally, the server comes equipped with 307 GB of local SSD storage and is premium storage capable, running under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark evaluations indicate average performance across several key workloads. The server achieves a stress-ng single-core CPU score of 1822.39 and a multi-core score of 14512.61. Memory performance is characterized by a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 565.91 GB/sec, though uncached large block write bandwidth drops to 41.29 GB/sec. In database and web serving tests, the instance demonstrates solid capabilities, delivering 10.92 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and 8.73 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. However, certain tasks like single-threaded bzip3 decompression and Geekbench text processing show weaker performance profiles.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ARM64 architecture offers a resource-dense profile that balances compute and memory without the premium cost of traditional x86 architectures. The inclusion of a 307 GB local SSD adds value for workloads requiring fast temporary storage. This server is well-suited for general-purpose workloads, including static web serving, software compilation, database operations, and lightweight text generation tasks.
